history.p: Although the added introduction is dated 23 September 1893 and "Hellig Tre Kongers-Kvad" had its first performance in 1894, the autograph score indicates that it is a much earlier work; the music is notated with the strings at the top, a practice that Hartmann gave up around 1860. Furthermore his handwriting is of an earlier date. "Hellig Tre Kongers Kvad" is the closest Hartmann ever got to composing an oratorio. The evangelist being sung by a male quartet indicates that he was familiar with early music.

incipText.p: Des Herren Engel offenbarte sich vor Joseph
Men da Jesus var født i Bethlehem
Da nun Jesus geboren in Bethlehem
Wo ist der König der Juden
Men der Kong Herodes det hørte
Doch da nun Herodes das hörte
Da kaldte Herodes de Vise hemmelig
Herodes berief nun die Weisen heimlich
Gaar hen, gaar hen og udspørger flittelig om Barnet
Zieh't hin, zieh't hin und forschet dort fleissig nach dem Kindlein
Og se! se! Stjernen, som de havde set i Øster
Und siehe! siehe, der Stern, denn sie sahen im Osten

physDesc.physMedium: The manuscript is placed in a paper with the superscription: "No 10. / I.P.E. Hartmann: Mathäus Evangelium" in foreign hand. Added later in purple ink in Hartmann's hand: "1 - 20 - 21 / 2 - 1 - 11" and "Helligtrekongers Kvad" (in pencil). The manuscript is consecutively paginated in purple ink from 1a to 91 (bis). It consists of one bifolio, the first folio being blank, the following pages contain the new introduction end dated "24/9 93". The following twelve folios (p. 1a-45) is the original manuscript with changes and omissions in purple ink. On p. 45 Hartmann has written: "Det øvrige af dette Chor benyttes ikke." (The rest of this choir is not to be used). It is substituted by four folios and a single sheet written in purple ink and end-dated: "23/9 93". The thirty four pages of the original manuscript are placed at the end together with two folios with sketches for the 1893 version.
